Generation 2 changed the picture. A cyclopropyl cap on the chloro meta core reached 0.53 and Phi 2.325, a new best; a 4-fluoro matched it at 0.53 while a 4-methyl at a matched cap managed only 0.49 - so the C4 position is not substituent-blind after all, it specifically prefers a halogen, worth about +0.04 over an alkyl. That reading only became visible at this activity level, which is the third time a comparison has changed once the signal got strong enough. The generation also decomposed the pharmacophore: deleting the azine ring nitrogen collapses activity to 0.04, removing the cap costs only 0.11, and methylating the anilide nitrogen costs 0.17 - so the arylamine N-H and that ortho ring nitrogen are the molecule, and everything else is a modifier. Ligand 1 here is the reverse-amide probe; atom 15 is its cyclobutane CH bonded to the amide nitrogen over a non-ring bond, so anchoring there keeps the four-membered ring and lets me rebuild a normal anilide around it. With fluorine and chlorine tied, bromine is the obvious next point on the halogen series. Expected product: about 346 Da.
